limitations: Approval is for revision 2 as a preimplementation specification with explicit evidence dispositions. It is not a production implementation, source-audit, native-runtime, or final delivery pass.

Both design scopes were reviewed against the preserved original design. No business production source, business screenshots, business cache/source trees, prior study outputs, or native SDK execution was used.

The original three review findings are prospectively resolved: nine added native rules cover required visible content, submitted acknowledgment disabled state, and notes availability in the existing six checkpoints; unexecuted callback branches have separate mandatory source-review obligations and explicit runtime limits.

The reconstructed verifier passes at design seal SHA256 cf692dbe3a5929babc55ab4ec550de25bad5cc5684873af3c52bd36bb5c6c419. Each platform has 34 rules, six states, 163 applicable assertions, 41 explicit N/A cells, and 18 indexed native obligations. All native assertions are owned; this does not mean any runtime assertion has passed.

All 55 source-only audit IDs per scope resolve to exact typed reference expectations and are owned by eight source-review obligations. The 48 original style values remain unchanged. A matching declaration or modifier application cannot establish computed font, color, padding, effective layout, or runtime use.

Native requirement_routes admission alone cannot establish complete acceptance. The approved design explicitly requires the conjunction of independent complete native/visual acceptance, independent source review passing every must obligation with real production file/line evidence, and the separate minimum-iOS module/client typecheck. Source review cannot close native unknowns or failures.

Closing notes, choosing self after delegate, acknowledgment false, self submission, same-choice quietness, and disabled-callback guards receive source inspection only under the selected route. No actual dispatch, callback interval, resulting rendering, or runtime quietness for those branches may be inferred from another transition.

Choice-content assertions require both exact caller substrings in the native Button label and allow native punctuation between them. They establish the specified native label content, not generic text style, glyph geometry, or independent physical touch behavior.

The iOS observer host targets iOS 17 and a later simulator. The complete real module and original public caller still require the separate iOS 14 compiler check; source review and later typechecking do not prove iOS14 runtime rendering.

The original API, bridge bytes, caller inputs, business action sequence, environments, style values, pixel sampling policy, and schematic drawings are preserved. The new collection.unavailable identifier names a conditional explanation already required by the original prose.

The observer capability preflight, fresh production captures, visual judgments, and app-level E2E remain later work. Android semantic OnClick is not OS touch; generic SwiftUI computed style, physical OS hit area, and real-app navigation/lifecycle remain outside these component observations.

All 139 candidate-v10 SDK-free tests passed again. They validate tool boundaries and synthetic evidence handling, not native capability or business production behavior. The original needs_revision review remains sealed and unchanged in design-review.
